title: Entanglement free Metrology Exploiting Multimode Hong Ou Mandel Sensor Advantage
abstract: The Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interference in the multimode frequency domain has been widely used in precision metrology, benefiting from robustness against dispersion and phase noise, as well as a large dynamic range and compatibility with fragile samples. Conventional multimode HOM metrology exploits frequency-entangled states, which naturally satisfy bosonic exchange symmetry under any centered symmetric joint spectral distribution, to provide these advantages. However, these entangled states are typically generated via spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC), requiring strong pump lasers that hinder practical implementation. In this paper, we employ frequency product states, which do not possess entanglement or path-mode exchange symmetry, as the probe state and post-select measurement outcomes exhibiting frequency anti-correlation. Our results demonstrate that these metrological advantages arise neither from entanglement nor from bosonic exchange symmetry, but rather from spectral anti-correlation
summary: This paper shows that the superior performance of Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interferometry, typically associated with quantum entanglement, can be achieved using simple frequency product states. By employing post-selection measurements, the authors demonstrate that the essential resource is effective frequency anti-correlation, not entanglement itself. This offers a more practical physical mechanism for high-precision quantum sensing.
main_problem: To demonstrate that the metrological advantages of Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interference can be achieved without relying on quantum entanglement.
main_result: The key metrological advantages (dispersion cancellation, wide dynamic range) are reproduced using frequency product states and post-selection, showing the resource is effective frequency anti-correlation, not entanglement.
method: The authors compare the coincidence probability derived from entangled states versus product states, utilizing post-selection measurements and analyzing the resulting Fisher Information.
model_or_system: The system involves Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interference measurements using either spectrally entangled biphoton states (from SPDC) or frequency product states as the input probe.
key_observables: Coincidence probability $P_c(\omega, \omega')$, Quantum Fisher Information ($F_Q$), and Classical Fisher Information ($F_{cl,post}$).
important_parameters: Spectral width ($\sigma$), sample delay ($	au$), and dispersion coefficients ($ eta_2$).
main_assumptions: The method relies on post-selection to extract anti-diagonal components, and the analysis of noise uses first-order phase noise approximations.
figures_summary: Figures simulate the spectral correlation map $P_c(\omega, \omega')$ showing the anti-diagonal selection line, and the resulting Fourier transform in the spatial domain, confirming the reproduction of the HOM interference pattern.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the conventional entangled HOM scheme, then proposes and analyzes the product-state scheme, demonstrating the reproduction of key features like peak narrowing and dispersion robustness, and finally compares the ultimate precision limits using Fisher Information.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial theoretical insight into the necessary quantum resources for high-precision sensing, suggesting that spectral correlations alone can mimic entanglement-enhanced performance in specific physical setups.
